Overview Reference Playground

@xufa/template

Templates of text and HTML with the safe expressions of @xufa/expression: values escaped for HTML, blocks, filters, partials, layouts and streaming, compiled once and rendered many times. With the plugin, reply.view() renders the views of a folder in @xufa/http (and fastify). It renders faster than Handlebars, Mustache, Nunjucks and even Eta and EJS, which run the JavaScript of their templates. No dependencies outside xufa.

Quick start

npm install @xufa/template   # or: import from 'xufa/template'
import { compile, render } from '@xufa/template';

const items = [
  { name: 'Pen', price: 5 },
  { name: 'Book', price: 12.5 },
];
const user = { name: 'Ada' };

const page = compile(`
<h1>{{ title | upper }}</h1>
<ul>
  {{~#each items as item~}}
  <li class="{{ loop.first ? 'first' : '' }}">{{ item.name }}: {{ item.price | number('en-US', { style: 'currency', currency: 'USD' }) }}</li>
  {{~else~}}
  <li>Nothing yet</li>
  {{~/each~}}
</ul>
{{#if user}}Hello, {{ user.name }}{{else}}<a href="/login">Log in</a>{{/if}}`);

console.log(page({ title: 'Books', items, user }));
console.log(render('Hello {{ name }}', { name: '<Ada>' })); // escaped
<h1>BOOKS</h1>
<ul><li class="first">Pen: $5.00</li><li class="">Book: $12.50</li></ul>
Hello, Ada
Hello &lt;Ada&gt;

API

FunctionWhat it does
compile(source, { name, escape })A function of the context that gives the text. Kept by source. render.stream(context) gives it in chunks; with one tag alone, render.value(context) gives its value.
render(source, context, options)compile(source, options)(context).
fill(value, context)Data with templates.
new TemplateEngine(options)An engine of its own; the module's functions use a default one.
pluginThe plugin of reply.view.
SafeString, escapeHtml, FILTERS, TemplateErrorHTML already safe, the escaping, the default filters, the errors.

Values

TagWrites
{{ expression }}The value, escaped for HTML.
{{{ expression }}}The value as it is.
{{ value | filter(args) | other }}The value through filters.

Expressions are those of @xufa/expression: {{ items.map(i => i.name).join(', ') }}, {{ `${count} items` }}, {{ user?.name ?? 'guest' }}. In templates they are lenient: a name that is not there, or a member of null, is nothing (strict: true makes them errors). null and undefined are written as nothing, lists and plain objects as JSON, the rest as text.

if

{{#if cart.items.length > 10}}
  <p>Free shipping!</p>
{{else if cart.items.length > 0}}
  <p>{{ 10 - cart.items.length }} more for free shipping</p>
{{else}}
  <p>Your cart is empty</p>
{{/if}}

each

{{#each orders as order, i}}
  <tr class="{{ loop.last ? 'last' : '' }}"><td>{{ loop.number }}</td><td>{{ order.id }}</td></tr>
{{else}}
  <tr><td>No orders</td></tr>
{{/each}}

{{#each settings as value, key}}{{ key }}={{ value }} {{/each}}

Lists, strings, iterables, Maps and plain objects (the second name is the index or the key; item is the name when none is given). loop has index, number (from 1), first, last, length and key. {{else}} is rendered when there is nothing. Inside, the names around the block are still there.

with

{{#with order.customer.address as address}}{{ address.street }}, {{ address.city }}{{/with}}

Partials

const engine = new TemplateEngine({ partials: { card: '<div class="card">{{ name }}</div>' } });
engine.partial('row', '<tr><td>{{ item.name }}</td></tr>');
engine.render('{{#each items as item}}{{> row}}{{/each}}{{> card user}}', { items, user });

{{> name}} renders a partial with the context; {{> name value}} with the properties of the value over it. Partials can be recursive (trees), up to maxDepth (32). With the plugin, partials are files of the folder: {{> partials/header}}.

Extends and blocks

As Django's {% extends %} and {% block %}: a base names its blocks (their contents are the defaults), and a template that extends it ({{extends 'name'}}, its first tag) fills those it wants; {{ block.super }} writes the contents of the one it extends. Chains of them (a page extends the base of its section, which extends that of the site), blocks in blocks, and {{/block name}} to say which one closes. The texts out of the blocks of a template that extends another are not written. The base is found as partials are (with the plugin: a file of the folder; give such views layout: false). As Django's {% extends variable %}, {{extends layout}} takes the name an expression gives when it renders ({{extends layout ?? 'base'}}): the built-in templates of @xufa/views extend the app's base so. app.hasView(name) says whether a view is a file of the folders. 

const engine = new TemplateEngine({
  partials: {
    base: '<title>{{#block title}}Library{{/block}}</title><nav>{{#block sidebar}}Home{{/block}}</nav>{{#block content}}{{/block}}',
    'catalog/base': "{{extends 'base'}}{{#block title}}Catalog - {{ block.super }}{{/block}}",
  },
});
const page = engine.compile(`{{extends 'catalog/base'}}
{{#block title}}{{ book.title }} | {{ block.super }}{{/block}}
{{#block sidebar}}{{ block.super }}, Books{{/block}}
{{#block content}}<h1>{{ book.title }}</h1>{{/block content}}`);
console.log(page({ book: { title: 'Emma' } }));
<title>Emma | Catalog - Library</title><nav>Home, Books</nav><h1>Emma</h1>

Comments and white space

{{! a comment }}
{{!-- a comment that can hold }} --}}
<ul>
  {{~#each items as item~}}   ~ takes out the white space before and after the tag
  <li>{{ item }}</li>
  {{~/each~}}
</ul>
\{{ not a tag }}               a backslash writes {{

Filters

FilterGives
upper, lower, capitalize, trimText changed.
default(fallback)The fallback for null, undefined and ''.
truncate(length, end = '…'), replace(search, replacement), slice(start, end)Text (or lists, for slice).
join(separator), length, first, last, reverse, keys, valuesOf lists, strings and objects.
round(digits), fixed(digits)Numbers.
number(locale, options), date(locale, options)Intl.NumberFormat and Intl.DateTimeFormat.
json(indent), urlencodeJSON, URI components.
escape, safeHTML escaped, or HTML as it is (a SafeString).
 
const engine = new TemplateEngine({ filters: { money: (value) => `${value.toFixed(2)} €` } });
engine.filter('initials', (name) => name.split(' ').map((part) => part[0]).join(''));
engine.render('{{ total | money }} by {{ user.name | initials }}', { total: 12, user: { name: 'Ada Lovelace' } });

reply.view

The plugin renders views, files of a folder, as @fastify/view does, on @xufa/http or fastify: 

import xufa from 'xufa';
import * as template from 'xufa/template';

const app = xufa();
app.register(template.plugin, { root: 'views', layout: 'layout', defaultContext: { site: 'Books' } });
app.addHook('preHandler', async (request, reply) => {
  reply.locals = { user: request.user }; // in the context of every view of the request
});
app.get('/books/:id', async (request, reply) => reply.view('books/show', { book: await findBook(request.params.id) }));

const html = await app.view('emails/welcome', { user }); // the text, for emails
DecorationWhat it does
reply.view(name, data, { layout, stream })Renders <root>/<name>.html and sends it as text/html, unless the reply has a content type.
reply.viewAsync(...), app.view(...)The text.
reply.localsNames for the views of the request, set in hooks.

The context of a view is defaultContext, then reply.locals, then the data. A name that leads out of root (.., an absolute path, in views and partials) is refused, so a view named by a request cannot read other files; a view that is not there, or fails, is an error (500) that names its template, line and column.

Layouts

<!-- views/layout.html -->
<!doctype html>
<html><head><title>{{ title ?? site }}</title></head>
<body>{{> partials/nav}}<main>{{ body }}</main></body></html>

The view is rendered first and given to its layout as body. The layout of the plugin, or of a call; layout: false for none. Pages whose parts change by page (a sidebar, the title) extend a base instead.

The context of every view

What every page shows (the user, the links of the sidebar, the CSRF token of its forms) comes from functions of the request, as Django's context processors: context of the plugin, and app.viewContext(fn) of other plugins (the accounts of @xufa/auth add user and perms). Each runs for every reply.view(), and may be async. 

app.register(template.plugin, {
  root: 'views',
  layout: 'layout',
  context: [async (request) => ({ cart: await Cart.of(request), year: new Date().getFullYear() })],
});
<a href="{{ url('book-detail', book.pk) }}">{{ book.title }}</a>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="{{ staticUrl('css/site.css') }}">
<form method="post"><input type="hidden" name="_csrf" value="{{ csrfToken }}">...</form>
{{#each messages as message}}<p class="{{ message.level }}">{{ message.text }}</p>{{/each}}
{{#if request.path === '/'}}...{{/if}}

With builtins (true), every view of a request has request (path, url, query, method), url(name, ...params) (the named routes), staticUrl(path) (with xufa.staticFiles), csrfToken and messages (of @xufa/session). The order: defaultContext, the builtins, the functions, reply.locals, then the data of the call. app.view() has no request: no context of requests.

Large pages

reply.view(name, data, { stream: true }), or stream: true for every view, sends the view in chunks made as the client reads them: the first bytes go at once, and the page is never whole in memory. The layout is cut where it writes {{ body }}: its head goes first, then the chunks of the view, then its tail. A page of 200,000 rows (20 MB) sends its first byte in 2 ms instead of 265, ends in 127 ms instead of 286, and takes 3 MB of memory instead of 40 (Benchmarks). 

app.get('/report', (request, reply) => reply.view('report', { rows: allRows }, { stream: true }));

for (const chunk of compile(source).stream(context, { chunkSize: 16384 })) socket.write(chunk); // any template

The files are read and compiled before anything is sent, so a view that is not there is still a 500; an error while the view renders cuts the response (its status is sent already). A layout that writes its body otherwise (twice, or through a filter) is rendered whole.

Options of the plugin

OptionDefaultWhat it does
root'views'The folder of the views.
extension'.html'Added to names without one.
layoutnoneThe view each view is rendered in, as body.
defaultContext{}The context of every view.
cacheNODE_ENV === 'production'Files read once; without it, every render reads them, so edits are seen at once (templates are compiled again only when they changed).
stream, chunkSizefalse, 65536Every view sent in chunks, of that many characters.
propertyName'view'The name of the decorations.
context[]Functions of (request, reply): the values of every view of a request (The context of every view).
builtinstruerequest, url(), staticUrl(), csrfToken and messages in every view of a request.
enginea new oneA TemplateEngine of your own; or its options (filters...) here.

Data with templates

const config = fill(
  {
    host: '{{ env.DB_HOST }}',
    port: '{{ Number(env.DB_PORT ?? 5432) }}',
    url: 'postgres://{{ env.DB_HOST }}/app',
    replicas: '{{ (env.REPLICAS ?? "").split(",").filter(Boolean) }}',
  },
  { env: process.env }
); // { host: 'db', port: 5432, url: 'postgres://db/app', replicas: ['r1', 'r2'] }

fill(value, context) fills the strings of data (configuration, messages) without escaping: a string that is one {{ expression }} alone gives its value (a number, a list, an object), the others their text; arrays and plain objects are filled item by item, and a key __proto__ of JSON stays a key.

Escaping

& < > " ' and the backtick are escaped, which makes values safe in the text of elements and in quoted attributes; not in <script>, in style, nor in URLs (href="{{ url }}" with javascript:...): check those values before they go there. escape: false (an engine, or one call) writes values as they are, and a function of your own escapes for other formats. new SafeString(html) marks text that is HTML already.

Engines

OptionDefaultWhat it does
escapetrueHTML escaping; false, or a function of the text.
filters, partials{}Over the default filters; sources of partials by name.
globals, builtins{}, trueThe globals of the expressions.
strictfalseNames not given and members of null are errors.
maxDepth32Partials in partials.
cacheSize500Templates compiled kept.
inlinetrueTemplates rendered often become one function, with their paths read inline.
loadPartial(name)The source of a partial that is not registered (the plugin reads them from files).

engine.filter(name, fn) and engine.partial(name, source) add filters and partials.

Errors

TemplateError, with code (XUFA_TEMPLATE_ERR_SYNTAX, XUFA_TEMPLATE_ERR_RUNTIME, XUFA_TEMPLATE_ERR_PARTIAL, or XUFA_EXPR_ERR_FORBIDDEN), the name of the template, line and column: 

TemplateError: {{#if}} is not closed (page.html, line 12, column 5)

Templates start as closures; the parts of a template rendered often become one function of JavaScript, with their paths ({{ user.name }}) read inline from names the expression engine checked, so templates rendered a few times do not pay for making it. Every case is in Benchmarks.

TypeScript

import { compile, TemplateEngine, RenderView, ReplyView } from '@xufa/template';

declare module '@xufa/http' {
  interface XufaInstance { view: RenderView }
  interface XufaReply { view: ReplyView<XufaReply>; viewAsync: RenderView; locals: Record<string, unknown> | null }
}
